title: FAMa Launches Counter-Operation in Mopti Following Twin Village Massacres — ~12 JNIM Fighters Killed in Targeted Strike Near Korikori/Gomossogou
detail: In response to JNIM's twin village massacres at Korikori and Gomossogou (night of May 6–7, 2026), the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) launched what it described as a 'targeted operation' in the Mopti Region area, neutralizing approximately a dozen JNIM fighters. The operation was confirmed in Al Jazeera reporting on the massacres. The counter-operation reflects FAMa's standard pattern following major JNIM attacks in the Mopti Region: a rapid follow-up air or ground engagement in the attack corridor before JNIM disperses. However, the tactical counter-operation addresses only the immediate fighters involved, not JNIM's structural capacity in the region — which has grown continuously since 2015 under Katiba Macina leadership. As of May 9, 2026, the broader crisis context remains unchanged: JNIM retains siege-interdiction capacity around Bamako; the Kenieroba prison situation remains unresolved; and the Alliance of Sahel States continues to mobilize but has not yet demonstrated operational capability to dislodge JNIM's hold on central Mali's rural corridors. International analysts and media published significant strategic assessments on May 9: African Arguments published 'Bamako under Siege: How Coordinated Attacks Exposed Mali's Fragility — and Tested the AES,' and the Council on Foreign Relations published 'Mali Is the Linchpin of West Africa — Now It's Under Jihadist Siege,' marking a significant escalation in Western institutional engagement with the crisis. Independent casualty figures for the FAMa counter-operation cannot be verified; FAMa figures are self-reported and consistently overstated in analogous past operations.
